requiredFindings.title: The write gate rechecks omit custody and required file owners
requiredFindings.failureScenario: After the creator releases its lock, the invocation acquires the installation fence and rechecks the account, the I-parent name, I and the fence. I's mode or ACL, or the fence file's owner, has changed. Item 3 still takes I's barrier and the I-parent barrier and continues the write. Owner §5 requires those custody and file-owner rechecks before and after the barriers, while the fence is held, and a failure latches the invocation. The same item also runs that recheck after a busy fence, where the lock was not acquired.

requiredFindings.title: Request-rejected creator codes omit the D9 error code, and several refusals have no row
requiredFindings.failureScenario: CORE.NO_EMBEDDED_RELEASE and INSTALLATION.ACCOUNT_REFUSED are request-rejected exit 2 with no D9ErrorCode, so one implementation emits REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED and another emits EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED. A NotPerformed rename, a pre-rename validation failure, a core refusal other than a missing embedded release, and a platform refusal such as an unqualified home filesystem have no row. Item 6 forbids a fourth domain detail, so those refusals are reported as HOST.IO_FAILURE or an NT-TCB detail and the caller follows the wrong remedy.

scope: Law 468 r1: existing-root admission after creation, the durable write gate, doctor completeness, and the public routes for creator failures. Items 2, 6, 7 and 9 are owner decisions.
